ratings.note: Desktop-only (minority device); empty right half is visual, the forms work. s=1.

Every basket visit (screenshot shows Wed 28 first, Sat 10 last); arrow keys move opposite to the visual order so wrong-session picks are possible. s=4, rated 3 because every card is fully dated and the confirm page restates the session, so a wrong pick is catchable before commit.
Desktop short pages only; visual finish issue with no task effect. s=1.
Rare combination (forced colours at 320 px), but for those users open days are indistinguishable and closed days are accepted, so a wrong day is likely; recurs every visit. s=3.
Use scene is short bursts while doing something else, so 10-minute expiry is common; the generic message gives no cause or remedy. s=3.
Only searches for unstocked tools; full list under the query is misleading but a sighted member will likely notice no sewing machine is listed. s=2.
Dark mode is common among members; inverted emphasis on availability badges causes misreading but text still states the date. s=2.
Filter panel only; native controls work and the date mask is a style/format inconsistency rather than a task obstacle. s=1.
Only on accidental taps; a slip means re-finding the tool and re-entering day and loan length (probe 42 shows empty basket after one tap). s=2.
Dark mode in the evening is the declared main scene; 3.07:1 text on availability badges fails 1.4.3 and is not overcome by learning, hard for older members. s=3.
Every reservation meets the newest-first session list; scanning cost and wrong-week risk. s=3.
Phones are the main device; the two drills read identically, recoverable by opening a card. s=2.
Screen-reader users navigating by heading lose grouping; content still reachable. s=2.
Desktop only; cards wrap but stay readable in the screenshot; ordering harm is rated under the reversed-order finding. s=1.

Every completed reservation; basket still lists the drill after confirming, inviting confusion or a duplicate. s=4, rated 3 because the done page itself clearly says 'Reservation confirmed' with a reference.
Every reservation re-asks the session with nothing preselected; extra decision and an error round-trip on the critical path. s=3.
Seen on every page but no task effect; brand expression only. s=1.
Lower-case, missing hyphen and spaced/+44 phone formats are common; correct numbers are rejected and the member must guess the layout. s=3.
Returning members, a few times a year; retyping and re-finding is effort, not a blocker. s=2.
Most calendar days are non-sessions and nothing prevents choosing them; error surfaces late or not at all. s=3.
Needs a second tap within 1.5 s (likely given no pending state); produces duplicate reservations and a desk query. s=3.
Misaligned value columns on every tool page; purely visual. s=1.
Desktop basket layout unevenness; readable. s=1.
Keyboard users who open the list; Esc fails but Enter on an option closes it. s=2.
Every reservation; redundant question and likely error round-trip before continuing. s=3.
Identifiers differ in digit count; mix-ups occasional and resolved at the desk. s=2.
Phone users looking for a specific drill; recoverable by opening one and going back. s=2.
Every keyboard/switch opening of the list; Tab and Shift+Tab are captured (2.1.2 trap), escape only by choosing an option. s=3.
Phone users wanting search scroll past ten cards; with only ten tools the list itself is scannable. s=2.
Every phone tool page: focused loan button and 'Two weeks' option sit behind the fixed bar (probe 13); recoverable by scrolling. s=3.
Every confirmation shows 'Basket (1)'; conflicting status and risk of re-reserving. s=3.
Only after leaving the confirm page mid-form; retyping from the card, recoverable. s=2.
Only for tools with later availability picked too early, but the reservation is confirmed and the member arrives to no tool (wasted trip). s=3.
Every card; identical placeholders give no visual cue when names are truncated. s=2.
Visual misalignment in the details list; no task effect. s=1.
Whenever session differs from tool day; contradictory dates are stored and the member may come on the wrong day. s=3.
Members wanting a date filter may miss the icon; dates are still on each card. s=2.
Desktop keyboard users; about ten extra tab stops each visit. s=2.
Stale or mistyped links only; wrong tool shown and reservable, though its name is visible. s=2.
Only members reserving more than three tools; partial refusal at the desk. s=2.
Every basket visit; hold time unknown to members who reserve in short bursts, leading to lost holds. s=3.
Members who chose a closed day learn only at Confirm and have no direct route back to the calendar. s=3.
Every use of Change in the core change-session journey; two collection dates at the commit step (probe 37). s=3.
Desktop short pages; visual only. s=1.
Screen-reader users pressing Reserve without a day hear a calendar date, not the error; silent failure for them. s=3.
Every confirmation; the content is complete and readable, lack of emphasis is aesthetic. s=1.
Screen-reader heading navigation flattened; basket names oversized for sighted users. s=2.
Both critical-path buttons on every reservation show no change for 1.2-1.5 s (probe 23/57), inviting repeat taps. s=3.
Phone users comparing drills; recoverable by opening a card. s=2.
Only when done.html is reopened without a stored reservation, but it shows a false confirmation number that leads to a desk contact. s=3.
Pauses over 10 minutes are common in the declared scene; after expiry Continue fails on every retry for the whole session, blocking the critical task. s=4.
Brand specificity only; no task effect. s=1.
Filter panel styling and date mask inconsistency; controls work. s=1.
Phone users; identical drill names and search below the list cost effort, recoverable. s=2.
First-time members (primary group) press 'Reserve this tool', get a 5 s toast and may leave believing it is reserved, then arrive to nothing (probe 10). One-time once learned. s=4.
Members typing a variant format; message repeats the empty-field text but its example hints at the fix. s=2.
Screen-reader users on every confirmation hear the first tool twice; confusing, not blocking. s=2.
Narrow cards cut the distinguishing end of names; recoverable by opening the card. s=2.
Phone users needing search scroll past the whole list; ten items keep it manageable. s=2.
Small phones and 200% zoom users (common among members) get horizontal scrolling on the main list with badges cut off; 1.4.10 failure. s=3.
Most days shown are non-sessions and several tools have later availability; invalid day accepted and carried into the basket (probes 32, 51). s=3.
Any no-match search leaves stale results presented as matches (probe 22 shows drills after 'sewing machine'); screen readers hear nothing. s=3.
Every card; placeholder thumbnails slow recognition by sight. s=2.
Nav labels wrap on phones but remain readable and tappable. s=1.
Keyboard users opening the list are trapped by Tab/Shift+Tab (2.1.2) until they choose an option. s=3.
Three of ten cards; colour carries unstated meaning, unavailable to colour-blind and screen-reader users, but the date text is present. s=2.
Every Change in the core journey; empty selection forces re-choosing and suggests loss. s=2.
